paras: YG’s debut studio album, My Krazy Life, released 18 March 2014 through CTE World, Pu$haz Ink and Def Jam, turned a Compton neighborhood story into a Billboard No. 2 debut on 61,000 first-week copies and was certified Platinum by the RIAA in 2017, with DJ Mustard’s West Coast production driving nearly every track.

Patchwerk’s own daily session reports show what that looked like from the inside: for five months starting in April 2013, Def Jam kept three rooms running for YG at once — Studio 9000 with engineer Dee Brown, and Studios 995 and 1019 with engineer Zane Shoemake — while DJ Mustard and, later, his in-house producer P-Lo made beats on site rather than bringing in finished tracks.

items.q: Where was YG’s My Krazy Life recorded?
items.a: YG recorded My Krazy Life at Patchwerk Recording Studios in Atlanta, Georgia. Patchwerk’s own daily session reports document 48 sessions for the album between April 2013 and March 2014, split across Studio 9000, Studio 995 and Studio 1019. Most of those sheets leave the Client line blank, but where it’s filled in it reads Def Jam Recordings, with a couple logged simply as YG.

items.q: Is it true YG ran three studios at once for My Krazy Life?
items.a: Yes — on 10 April 2013, three separate Patchwerk session reports show YG’s camp working simultaneously: Studio 995 with engineer Zane Shoemake and DJ Mustard making beats, Studio 9000 with engineer Dee Brown tracking “BPT” and Tory Lanez’s “All Over the Place,” and Studio 1019 with engineer Alverne Emmanuel tracking “Bompton” under producer FKI. All three sheets log the same overnight hours, roughly 6pm to sunrise.

items.q: Did DJ Mustard and P-Lo make beats at Patchwerk for My Krazy Life?
items.a: Yes. Patchwerk session reports name DJ Mustard making beats on site on 10 April 2013 and credit him as producer on sessions for “My Nigga,” “Sorry Momma” and others; client hard drives are repeatedly labeled “Mustard Drive” in the paperwork through the whole residency. P-Lo is separately logged making beats in Studio 1019 across two overnight sessions, 29–30 July 2013.

items.q: Who engineered My Krazy Life at Patchwerk?
items.a: Dee Brown engineered My Krazy Life at Patchwerk Recording Studios, logging 29 sessions — the largest share of the record by far, all but two of them in Studio 9000 (the other two in Studio 995). Zane Shoemake engineered 12 sessions split between Studio 995 and Studio 1019, and Alverne Emmanuel assisted on tracking dates in 1019. Kenneth “K. Rich” Richmond assisted a Dee Brown session in Studio 9000, and separately turns up as primary engineer in a room logged “1019 / 995” — the session moved rooms mid-take after the computer cut off.

YG’s “My Nigga” (feat. Rich Homie Quan & Jeezy) was first tracked at Patchwerk Recording Studios on 11 April 2013, in Studio 995 with DJ Mustard producing and Zane Shoemake engineering a sixteen-hour overnight session, 6pm to 10am. The song was worked twice more that year, on 14 May and 30 July, before the album released the following March.

items.q: Did Patchwerk host a listening session before My Krazy Life came out?
items.a: Yes — a Patchwerk session report from 4 March 2014, Studio 9000, logs a “Listening Party” with engineer Dee Brown, two weeks before My Krazy Life released on 18 March 2014. It closes out the album’s Patchwerk paper trail, nearly a year after the first session in the same room.

sections.intro: Ten of the album’s fourteen tracks are named directly in Patchwerk’s daily session reports — the count after each title is how many separate sessions logged that song between April 2013 and March 2014. “Momma Speech Intro,” “I Just Wanna Party,” “Do It to Ya” and “1AM” don’t appear by name on any Patchwerk sheet and aren’t listed here.

sections.intro: Drawn from the studio’s daily session reports. Three sheets in this run were photographed twice and are counted once here.

items.what: The residency opens: a beatmaking session in 1019 while “The Homie” is tracked overnight in 9000 — DJ Mustard’s own beatmaking date at Patchwerk follows two nights later, in Studio 995.
Three rooms running the same overnight hours: DJ Mustard making beats in 995, “BPT” and Tory Lanez’s “All Over the Place” tracked in 9000, “Bompton” tracked in 1019.
items.who: Zane Shoemake · Dee Brown · Alverne Emmanuel · 6pm–dawn

items.what: “My Nigga” (feat. Rich Homie Quan & Jeezy) tracked in a sixteen-hour overnight session, DJ Mustard producing.
“Me & My Bitch” tracked — a Tory Lanez hook, live violins, and a hook for “Boyz N Da Hood.”
“Me & My Bitch” and the working title “Ghetto” tracked across two overnight sessions.
“My Nigga” revisited alongside working titles “Hella Ice” and “My Niggas.”
P-Lo making beats on site across two sessions — the first overnight, the second an evening date — working from a client laptop.
“Really Be (Smokin N Drinkin)” tracked, TY$ producing, in a thirteen-hour overnight session; a Complex Media interview and video shoot ran in the same room earlier that afternoon.
“Really Be,” “Who Do You Love?” and “Sorry Momma” all tracked in one 14.5-hour day.
“Thank God” and “Bicken Back Being Bool” tracked.
Three rooms again: beats arranged in 1019, keyboard tracked in 995, and “Sorry Momma” finished in 9000 with DJ Mustard and Terrace Martin producing.
A single-deal session logged as “Freaky Dance” — the last of the main residency.
A listening party, two weeks before the album’s release.

sections.body: My Krazy Life is the sound of a label moving in. For five months in 2013, Def Jam ran three Patchwerk rooms at once for one artist — DJ Mustard and P-Lo making beats down the hall while Dee Brown and Zane Shoemake tracked vocals in the rooms next door.

note: Engineering credits shown are drawn directly from Patchwerk’s own session logs for this record; only Patchwerk’s documented contributions are listed here.
